stories.title: Tense negotiations in Washington to end partial government shutdown
stories.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson predicts the partial shutdown will be over by Tuesday.

stories.title: What does normal look like in Caracas one month after the Maduro operation?
stories.summary: Nearly a month after U.S. forces seized Nicolás Maduro, Caracas is settling into an uneasy normal, with major changes and lingering questions about what lasts and what comes next.

stories.title: Minnesota woman says local police freed her from immigration agents' custody
stories.summary: A Minnesota woman says that after she filmed immigration agents, the officers chased her, detained her at gunpoint, and later dropped her off with local police.

stories.title: Doctors say measures to control an incurable lung disease aren't enough
stories.summary: Silicosis is an often deadly lung disease linked to inhaling toxic dust from cutting engineered stone. California has passed new safety measures for workers in the last few years, but doctors say they aren't enough.

stories.title: Faith leaders in Memphis join together to support Afghan refugees
stories.summary: Two Memphis pastors, Stephen Cook and Latif Salar, are working to protect Afghan church members after the Trump administration halted asylum processing.

stories.title: Hollywood takes some shortcuts when it comes to depicting Americans abroad
stories.summary: An NPR panel looks at how movies portray Americans abroad, from romantic self discovery to culture clash and stereotypes.
